title: Formal or casual: register in emails and speech
summary: Choose between tú and usted, soften requests, write a formal email and recognise casual Spanish from Spain.
focus: Matching register: usted and formal email formulas vs colloquial Spanish from Spain
content:
## Tú or usted?

**Usted** is the polite *you*. It takes the third-person verb and the pronouns **le** and **su**. Use it with strangers, clients, older people, officials and anyone you write a formal letter to. **Tú** is for friends, family, children and, in Spain, most colleagues, often the boss too.

| tú | usted |
|---|---|
| ¿Tienes un momento? | ¿Tiene un momento? |
| Te escribo para… | Le escribo para… |
| tu correo | su correo |
| Siéntate. | Siéntese. |

When in doubt, start with **usted** and let the other person offer **tú**: *¿Nos tuteamos?* (Shall we say tú?) **Tutear** means to address someone as tú; **hablar de usted** means to use usted.

## Softening a request

A bare command (**Mándeme el informe**) sounds blunt. Spanish softens a request by stepping back into the past or into the conditional:

- **Quería pedirle** un favor. (I wanted to ask you a favour; polite, not past)
- **Quisiera** hablar con la directora. (I would like to speak to the director.)
- **¿Podría** enviarme el horario? (Could you send me the timetable?)
- **¿Le importaría** esperar un momento? (Would you mind waiting a moment?)
- **¿Sería tan amable de** firmar aquí? (Would you be so kind as to sign here?)

**¿Le importaría que** + imperfect subjunctive asks for permission: *¿Le importaría que abriera la ventana?* (Would you mind if I opened the window?)

## The formal email

| Part | Formal | Informal |
|---|---|---|
| Greeting | **Estimado señor Gil:** / **Estimada Sra. Ruiz:** | **Hola, Ana:** |
| Purpose | **Le escribo para** solicitar información. | Te escribo para contarte… |
| Attachment | **Adjunto le envío** el currículum. | Te mando las fotos. |
| Before closing | **Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.** | Escríbeme pronto. |
| Sign-off | **Atentamente,** | **Un abrazo,** / **Besos,** |

The greeting ends with a colon, not a comma; to a company with no name, write **Estimados señores:**. **Un saludo** (or **Saludos**) sits in between. It is polite but friendly, right for colleagues and most work emails. **Atentamente** is for strangers, companies and officials.

## Casual Spain, and when each fits

These words are everyday spoken Spanish in Spain. They are colloquial and friendly, never for a formal email or a client.

- **vale**: OK, fine. *—¿A las ocho? —Vale.*
- **guay**: cool, great. *¡Qué guay!*
- **tío / tía**: mate, dude, between friends (literally *uncle / aunt*).
- **¡qué va!**: no way, not at all. *—¿Estás cansada? —¡Qué va!*
- **me mola**: I love it, I'm into it. *Me mola tu chaqueta.*

Match the other person. A job application, a complaint, a first email to a stranger: **usted** and the formal formulas. Colleagues: **tú** and **Un saludo**. Friends: **tú** and as much **vale** and **guay** as you like. Mixing the two (*Estimado tío*) sounds like a joke.

vocabulary.example: ¿Nos tuteamos? Somos compañeros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Shall we say tú to each other? We're colleagues.

vocabulary.example: ¿Le importaría repetir su apellido?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Would you mind repeating your surname?

vocabulary.meaning: to be so kind as to (formal request)
vocabulary.example: ¿Sería tan amable de indicarme la salida?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Would you be so kind as to show me the way out?

vocabulary.meaning: I wanted to ask you (polite, usted)
vocabulary.example: Quería pedirle un día libre el viernes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wanted to ask you for a day off on Friday.

vocabulary.meaning: dear (formal letters, followed by a colon)
vocabulary.example: Estimada señora Ortega:
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dear Mrs Ortega,

vocabulary.example: Le adjunto las facturas de enero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm attaching January's invoices.

vocabulary.meaning: to await, to look forward to (formal)
vocabulary.example: Quedamos a la espera de sus instrucciones.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We look forward to your instructions.

vocabulary.example: Atentamente, Carmen Ibáñez
vocabulary.example_meaning: Yours sincerely, Carmen Ibáñez

vocabulary.example: Gracias por todo. Un saludo, Pablo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Thanks for everything. Kind regards, Pablo.

vocabulary.example: Vale, te espero en la puerta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: OK, I'll wait for you at the door.

vocabulary.example: Tu piso nuevo es muy guay.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your new flat is really cool.

vocabulary.example: Tía, ¡cuánto tiempo sin verte!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Hey, it's been ages since I saw you!

vocabulary.meaning: no way, not at all (colloquial, Spain)
vocabulary.example: —¿Te molesta la música? —¡Qué va!
vocabulary.example_meaning: —Does the music bother you? —Not at all!

vocabulary.meaning: I love it, I'm into it (colloquial, Spain)
vocabulary.example: Me mola mucho este barrio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I really love this neighbourhood.

quiz.prompt: You are writing to a company for the first time and know nobody's name. Which greeting fits?
quiz.explanation: A formal email to an unknown company opens with Estimados señores: and a colon. ¡Hola, chicos! and ¿Qué tal, tío? are for friends.
hints: Formal letter, nobody's name: estimado + colon.

quiz.prompt: ___ le envío mi currículum. (adjuntar, yo: I attach)
quiz.explanation: Adjunto le envío… (I attach…) is the standard formal formula: adjuntar in the yo form.
hints: The yo form of adjuntar ends in -o.

quiz.prompt: You end a formal complaint to an airline. Which closing fits?
options: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,
quiz.correct_answer: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,
quiz.explanation: A complaint to a company is formal: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta (I look forward to your reply) and Atentamente. Hugs and tío are for friends.
hints: Su respuesta, not tu: the airline gets usted.

quiz.prompt: You write to the director of a museum you have never met. Which request fits?
options: ¿Sería tan amable de enviarme el programa?
quiz.correct_answer: ¿Sería tan amable de enviarme el programa?
quiz.explanation: A stranger in a formal email gets usted and a softened request: ¿Sería tan amable de…? The other two use tú and colloquial words.
hints: Look for usted and a polite formula.

quiz.prompt: ¿Le ___ cerrar la ventana? (importar, polite: Would you mind closing the window?)
quiz.explanation: ¿Le importaría + infinitive? asks politely. It is the conditional of importar in the usted (third-person) form.

quiz.prompt: Your friend Marta says: «Tu chaqueta nueva me mola, es muy guay.» What does she mean?
options: She really likes your new jacket.
She thinks your new jacket is too big.
She wants to borrow your new jacket.
quiz.correct_answer: She really likes your new jacket.
quiz.explanation: Me mola (I love it) and guay (cool) are colloquial Spanish from Spain: she is paying you a compliment.

quiz.prompt: Somos compañeros, ¿nos ___? (tutear, nosotros: Shall we say tú to each other?)
quiz.explanation: Tutear is a regular -ar verb: nosotros tuteamos. ¿Nos tuteamos? is how Spaniards offer to drop usted.

quiz.prompt: Señora Molina, quería ___ un favor. (pedir + le: I wanted to ask you a favour)
quiz.explanation: The pronoun le (to you, usted) is attached to the infinitive: quería pedirle. The imperfect quería softens the request.
¡Qué va! (not at all) denies what was asked; vale means OK and guay means cool, which make no sense as an answer here.
hints: He is saying no, he isn't angry.

conversations.title: First day at the studio
conversations.scenario: Elena Vidal starts as a designer at a small studio in Valencia and meets her manager, Andrés Prieto.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenos días. ¿Es usted el señor Prieto? Soy Elena Vidal, la nueva diseñadora.
lines.meaning: Good morning. Are you Mr Prieto? I'm Elena Vidal, the new designer.
lines.note: A stranger and a boss: she starts with usted.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Encantado, Elena. Pero llámame Andrés, por favor: aquí nos tuteamos todos.
lines.meaning: Nice to meet you, Elena. But call me Andrés, please: we all say tú here.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, perfecto. Entonces, ¿me enseñas dónde está mi mesa?
lines.meaning: OK, great. So, will you show me where my desk is?
lines.note: Offered tú, she switches at once.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro, junto a la ventana. ¿Has traído el contrato firmado?
lines.meaning: Sure, by the window. Have you brought the signed contract?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, y ayer también te lo adjunté en un correo.
lines.meaning: Yes, and yesterday I also attached it to an email for you.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ah, es verdad. Una cosa: a los clientes, siempre de usted.
lines.meaning: Oh, that's right. One thing: clients, always usted.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Entendido. «Estimado señor», «Le escribo para…» y «Un saludo».
lines.meaning: Understood. 'Dear Sir', 'I am writing to…' and 'Kind regards'.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Exacto. Y nada de «tío» ni «guay» en los correos, ¿eh?
lines.meaning: Exactly. And no 'mate' or 'cool' in the emails, OK?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué va! Eso solo se lo digo a mis amigos.
lines.meaning: No way! I only say that to my friends.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me parece genial. Bienvenida al equipo.
lines.meaning: Sounds great to me. Welcome to the team.

listening.text: ¡Qué va, no estoy enfadada!
listening.meaning: No way, I'm not angry!
listening.note: ¡Qué va! is colloquial and means not at all.

listening.text: ¿Le importaría hablar un poco más despacio?
listening.meaning: Would you mind speaking a little more slowly?

listening.text: Quería pedirle información sobre el curso de verano.
listening.meaning: I wanted to ask you for information about the summer course.
listening.note: Quería softens the request; it is not really past.

listening.text: Tío, el concierto de anoche fue muy guay.
listening.meaning: Mate, last night's concert was really cool.
listening.note: Colloquial Spanish from Spain, only with friends.

listening.text: Le escribo para reclamar el dinero de mi billete.
listening.meaning: I am writing to claim back the money for my ticket.
listening.note: New word: reclamar = to claim back.

listening.text: ¿Sería usted tan amable de firmar en la última página?
listening.meaning: Would you be so kind as to sign on the last page?

listening.text: Mi nueva jefa me pidió que la tuteara desde el primer día.
listening.meaning: My new boss asked me to call her tú from the first day.

listening.text: Quedamos a la espera de su respuesta y le enviamos un cordial saludo.
listening.meaning: We look forward to your reply and send you our warm regards.

guide.tip: Not sure which to use? Start with usted and wait: if they say «puedes tutearme», switch to tú.

bites.title: Tú or usted?
bites.rule: Usted (third-person verb, le, su) for strangers, clients, older people and formal letters; tú for friends, family and most colleagues in Spain. Wait to be offered tú.
bites.example_meaning: Excuse me, could you help me?

bites.title: Soften it
bites.rule: Wrap a request in quería, quisiera, ¿le importaría…? or ¿sería tan amable de…? The imperfect and the conditional make it sound less pushy.

bites.title: The formal email
bites.rule: Estimado/a + colon, Le escribo para…, Adjunto le envío…, Quedo a la espera de su respuesta, Atentamente. Un saludo is the friendlier, neutral close.
bites.example: Estimada señora Ruiz: le escribo para solicitar una cita.
bites.example_meaning: Dear Mrs Ruiz, I am writing to request an appointment.

bites.title: Casual Spain
bites.rule: Vale, guay, tío/tía, ¡qué va! and me mola are colloquial Spanish from Spain: great with friends, out of place with a client or in a formal email.

sorts.title: Formal or casual?
sorts.why: Formal formulas use usted and fixed phrases; vale, guay, tío, qué va and mola are casual words from Spain.

sorts.title: Tú or usted?
sorts.why: Usted takes the third-person verb and le/su; tú takes the second person and te/tu.

sorts.title: Where does it go in the email?
sorts.why: Estimado/a opens, le escribo and adjunto carry the message, Atentamente and Un saludo close.

spots.sentence: Estimado señor López: te escribo para pedir información.
spots.why: Estimado sets a formal tone: usted, so le escribo.
Le marks usted, which takes the third-person verb: importaría.

spots.sentence: Quedo a la espera de tu respuesta. Atentamente, Pablo Ruiz.
spots.why: A letter signed Atentamente uses usted: su respuesta.

spots.sentence: Adjunto te envío el informe, señor director.
spots.why: Señor director gets usted: Adjunto le envío.

spots.sentence: Perdone, ¿puedes decirme dónde está la estación?
spots.why: Perdone is usted, so keep it: ¿puede decirme…?

builds.meaning: I am writing to ask for information.
Would you mind waiting a moment?

builds.text: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
builds.meaning: I look forward to your reply.
Would you be so kind as to help me?

realm.content:
## El registro en Eldmark

At the court of Highgate you speak **de usted**: **Majestad, quisiera pedirle un favor**, **¿le importaría escucharme?** Letters to the guild open with **Estimados miembros del gremio:** and close with **Atentamente**. At the posada with your party it's **tú**, **vale**, **tío** and **¡qué va!**

vocabulary.example: Posadero, ¿le importaría guardar mi espada?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Innkeeper, would you mind looking after my sword?

vocabulary.example: Majestad, quería pedirle permiso para cazar en el Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your Majesty, I wanted to ask your permission to hunt in the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: Estimados miembros del gremio de cazadores:
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dear members of the hunters' guild,

vocabulary.example: Atentamente, Brena, cazadora de Frostmarch.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Yours faithfully, Brena, huntress of Frostmarch.

vocabulary.example: Vale, repartimos el botín a medias.
vocabulary.example_meaning: OK, we split the loot half and half.

vocabulary.example: ¿Miedo de los orcos? ¡Qué va!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Scared of the orcs? No way!

vocabulary.meaning: audience (a formal meeting with a ruler)
vocabulary.example: La reina concede audiencia los lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The queen grants audiences on Mondays.

vocabulary.example: Su Majestad la recibirá ahora.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Her Majesty will see you now.

vocabulary.example: La posadera nos tutea a todos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The innkeeper says tú to all of us.

bites.title: Court or tavern?
bites.rule: At court, with the guild or a stranger: usted, ¿le importaría…?, Atentamente. At the posada with your party: tú, vale, tío, ¡qué va!
bites.example_meaning: Your Majesty, I would like to ask you a favour.

listening.text: ¡Qué va, el orco no me asusta!
listening.meaning: No way, the orc doesn't scare me!

listening.text: Majestad, ¿le importaría escucharme un momento?
listening.meaning: Your Majesty, would you mind listening to me for a moment?

listening.text: Estimados miembros del gremio de magas:
listening.meaning: Dear members of the mages' guild,
listening.note: A formal letter opens with estimado and a colon.

listening.text: Tío, ¿cenamos algo en la posada?
listening.meaning: Mate, shall we have something to eat at the inn?

listening.text: Su Majestad la recibirá en audiencia mañana.
listening.meaning: Her Majesty will receive you in audience tomorrow.
listening.note: New word: la audiencia = the audience.

builds.meaning: Your Majesty, I would like to ask you a favour.
Would you mind watching my mount?

spots.sentence: Estimada maestra del gremio: te escribo para pedir una montura.
spots.why: Estimada opens a formal letter: usted, le escribo.

sorts.title: Court or tavern?
sorts.why: Court and guild letters take usted and fixed formulas; at the posada friends use tú and colloquial words.

quiz.prompt: Your audience with the queen of Highgate begins. Which line fits?
quiz.explanation: A queen in audience gets usted and a softened request: quisiera pedirle. Tía and oye with tú belong to the posada.

quiz.prompt: Posadero, ¿le ___ guardar mi espada? (importar, polite: Would you mind…?)
quiz.explanation: ¿Le importaría + infinitive? is the polite request. It uses the conditional in the usted form.

conversations.title: Court by day, tavern by night
conversations.scenario: Brena, a huntress from Frostmarch, asks Torvo, the dwarf chamberlain at the court of Highgate, for an audience; that night they meet at the posada, where they are old friends.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenos días, señora cazadora. ¿En qué puedo ayudarla?
lines.meaning: Good morning, huntress. How may I help you?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Quisiera pedir audiencia con Su Majestad, si es tan amable.
lines.meaning: I would like to request an audience with Her Majesty, if you would be so kind.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Su Majestad la recibirá mañana. ¿Le importaría dejar el arco en la puerta?
lines.meaning: Her Majesty will see you tomorrow. Would you mind leaving your bow at the door?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Por supuesto. Muchas gracias por su ayuda.
lines.meaning: Of course. Thank you very much for your help.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Brena! What's up? Not saying tú to me any more?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Qué va! En la corte, de usted; en la posada, de tú.
lines.meaning: No way! At court, usted; at the inn, tú.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, pues te invito a un pastel. ¿Te mola?
lines.meaning: OK, then the pie's on me. Fancy it?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me mola mucho. ¡Y mañana, otra vez de usted!
lines.meaning: I'd love that. And tomorrow, usted again!

meadowbrook.content:
## El registro en Meadowbrook

Nora writes to the mayor for a stall at the festival: **Estimado señor alcalde:**, **Le escribo para pedir un puesto**, **Adjunto le envío la solicitud**, **Atentamente**. At Rosa's seed shop or by the river with Leo, it's **tú**: **¡Vale!**, **¡Qué guay!**

vocabulary.example: Estimado señor alcalde:
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dear Mr Mayor,

vocabulary.example: Señor alcalde, ¿le importaría leer mi propuesta?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Mr Mayor, would you mind reading my proposal?

vocabulary.example: Adjunto le envío la solicitud firmada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Please find attached the signed application.

vocabulary.example: Atentamente, Nora, la nueva granjera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Yours sincerely, Nora, the new farmer.

vocabulary.example: Vale, Rosa, mañana te compro más semillas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: OK, Rosa, I'll buy more seeds from you tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: ¡Qué calabaza tan guay, Nora!
vocabulary.example_meaning: What a cool pumpkin, Nora!

vocabulary.example: Quisiera un puesto en el festival de otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I would like a stall at the autumn festival.

vocabulary.example: Mi propuesta es un concurso de calabazas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My proposal is a pumpkin contest.

vocabulary.example: La solicitud tiene dos páginas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The application form has two pages.

bites.title: Mayor or neighbour?
bites.rule: A letter to the alcalde takes usted: Estimado señor alcalde:, Le escribo para…, Atentamente. Rosa and Leo get tú, vale and ¡qué guay!
bites.example: Estimado señor alcalde: le escribo para pedir un puesto.
bites.example_meaning: Dear Mr Mayor, I am writing to ask for a stall.

listening.text: Vale, Rosa, nos vemos en la tienda.
listening.meaning: OK, Rosa, see you at the shop.

listening.text: Le escribo para pedir un puesto en el festival.
listening.meaning: I am writing to ask for a stall at the festival.
listening.note: New word: el puesto = the stall.

listening.text: ¡Qué guay, Leo! ¿Has pescado eso tú solo?
listening.meaning: How cool, Leo! Did you catch that all by yourself?

listening.text: Adjunto le envío mi propuesta para el concurso.
listening.meaning: Please find attached my proposal for the contest.
listening.note: New word: la propuesta = the proposal.

listening.text: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta, señor alcalde.
listening.meaning: I look forward to your reply, Mr Mayor.

builds.meaning: Would you mind reading my proposal?
Yours sincerely, Nora, the new farmer.

spots.sentence: Estimado señor alcalde: te escribo por el festival.
spots.why: A letter to the mayor takes usted: le escribo.

sorts.title: Mayor or neighbour?
sorts.why: The mayor's letter takes usted and formulas; neighbours and friends get tú and casual words.

quiz.prompt: Nora writes to the alcalde to ask for a stall at the festival. Which closing fits?
quiz.explanation: A formal letter to the mayor closes with Atentamente; besos and tío are for friends.
hints: The mayor is not her friend yet.

quiz.prompt: ___ le envío la solicitud para el festival. (adjuntar, yo: I attach)
quiz.explanation: Adjunto le envío… is the formal formula for an attachment: adjuntar in the yo form.
hints: The yo form of adjuntar ends in -o.

rustwake.content:
## El registro en el páramo

A message to el capataz Ruiz on the radiorreloj is formal: **Estimado capataz Ruiz:**, **quería pedirle permiso**, **¿sería tan amable de abrir la cúpula?** Trading tuercas with Marta la mercadera, it's **tú**: **vale, tía**, **¡qué va!**, **me mola tu armadura**.

vocabulary.example: Capataz, ¿sería tan amable de abrir la cúpula?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman, would you be so kind as to open the Dome?

vocabulary.example: Capataz Ruiz, quería pedirle más agua filtrada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz, I wanted to ask you for more filtered water.

vocabulary.example: Estimado capataz Ruiz:
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dear Foreman Ruiz,

vocabulary.example: ¿Miedo de la tormenta de ceniza? ¡Qué va!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Scared of the ash storm? No way!

vocabulary.example: Tía, ¿cuántas tuercas por esta gaseosa?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Hey, how many nuts for this soda?

vocabulary.example: Me mola tu armadura de chatarra, Leo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I love your scrap armour, Leo.

vocabulary.example: Necesito un permiso para salir al páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I need a permit to go out into the wasteland.

vocabulary.example: Le envío el informe sobre la antena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm sending you the report on the antenna.

bites.title: Foreman or trader?
bites.rule: To el capataz on the radiorreloj: usted, quería pedirle, ¿sería tan amable de…? With Marta at the market: tú, vale, tía, ¡qué va!
bites.example: Capataz, quería pedirle permiso para explorar.
bites.example_meaning: Foreman, I wanted to ask your permission to explore.

listening.text: ¡Qué va, tía, la cabra no muerde!
listening.meaning: No way, the goat doesn't bite!

listening.text: Vale, Marta, te cambio diez tuercas por agua.
listening.meaning: OK, Marta, I'll swap you ten nuts for water.
listening.note: With a trader friend, use tú.

listening.text: ¿Sería tan amable de reparar mi radiorreloj?
listening.meaning: Would you be so kind as to repair my wrist radio?

listening.text: Capataz, quería pedirle permiso para salir.
listening.meaning: Foreman, I wanted to ask your permission to go out.
listening.note: New word: el permiso = the permission.

listening.text: Tío, tu robot jardinero me mola mucho.
listening.meaning: Mate, I really love your gardener robot.

builds.text: ¿Sería tan amable de abrir la cúpula?
builds.meaning: Would you be so kind as to open the Dome?

builds.text: Vale, tía, te cambio agua por tuercas.
builds.meaning: OK, I'll swap you water for nuts.

spots.why: Perdone is usted, so keep it: ¿puede abrir…?

spots.sentence: Estimado capataz Ruiz: te envío el informe de la antena.

sorts.title: Foreman or trader?
sorts.why: The foreman gets usted and formulas; a trader friend gets tú and colloquial words.

quiz.prompt: You send a message to el capataz Ruiz asking him to open the Dome. Which line fits?
options: ¿Sería tan amable de abrir la cúpula?
quiz.correct_answer: ¿Sería tan amable de abrir la cúpula?
quiz.explanation: The foreman gets usted and a softened request: ¿Sería tan amable de…? The other two are casual tú.

quiz.prompt: —¿Te da miedo la tormenta de ceniza, Leo? —¡___! Ya he visto muchas. (colloquial: Not at all!)
quiz.explanation: ¡Qué va! is the colloquial Spanish way to say not at all.
